discovery: Detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian), USA

nominees.name: Will J. Percival
nominees.affiliation: University of Waterloo and Perimeter Institute, Canada

motivation: In 2005 the SDSS (Eisenstein et al.) and 2dFGRS (Cole, Percival et al.) teams independently found the imprint of sound waves in the primordial plasma in the clustering of galaxies. This feature is a characteristic scale of about 150 Mpc, set by physics already measured in the cosmic microwave background. The detection turned galaxy surveys into a geometric standard ruler. It confirmed that the large-scale structure we see today grew from the same perturbations seen in the CMB, and it provided a measurement of the expansion history that is robust to astrophysical systematics. The nominees went on to develop the theory, reconstruction methods and survey programmes (BOSS, eBOSS, DESI) that made BAO a precision tool. DESI's 2024–2025 results, which hint at evolving dark energy, show that this tool now tests ΛCDM directly. Few probes have so changed how we measure the Universe.
